title: The anchor-coverage check added 2026-08-09 makes every sentinel and darkocean run fail by construction — the observatory has notarized no new night since 2026-08-09
statement: verify.py's check_anchors (verify.py, lines 493-528) requires that every manifest matching the glob `*/**/snapshots/*/manifest.json` found ON DISK already appear in anchors/ledger.json (line 525-528: 'every register night must appear in the ledger, anchored or not'). sentinel.yml and darkocean.yml both run `python -m practice.foreknown.run` / `python -m practice.darkocean.run` (which write that run's own new manifest.json file to the working tree) and THEN run `python verify.py --repo-root .` in the same job, before the commit step (sentinel.yml 'Notarize announced futures' -> 'Verify provenance chain' -> 'Commit observation'; darkocean.yml 'Coverage-vs-Declaration reading' -> 'Verify provenance chain' -> 'Commit reading'). tools/anchor.py's own manifests() (tools/anchor.py, lines 76-81) globs the SAME pattern, but anchor.yml runs as a separate scheduled job (cron '20 6 * * *', after darkocean's '50 4 * * *' and sentinel's '45 5 * * *' per their own workflow comments) that checks out main FRESH and can only ever anchor a manifest that is already committed there. The two facts together are a structural deadlock: a night's own manifest cannot be in the anchor ledger before that night's sentinel/darkocean job has committed it, so check_anchors as written will refuse every run's own fresh manifest, forever, from the moment it started running. anchors/ledger.json currently lists exactly 6 manifests (darkocean 2026-08-07, 2026-08-08; foreknown 2026-08-08, 2026-08-09; foreknown/reaction 2026-08-08, 2026-08-09), all state 'complete' -- nothing dated 2026-08-10 or later, because nothing dated 2026-08-10 or later has ever been committed. foreknown/snapshots/ and darkocean/snapshots/ both stop at 2026-08-08/2026-08-09; there is no foreknown-notary-run, darkocean-run or foreknown-correct-* entry in autonomy/log.jsonl after 2026-08-09T14:50:39Z; the repository's last commit before this discovery pass is a8b1510 (2026-08-10T08:05:14Z, 'anchor:'), which only bumped anchors/ledger.json's own generated_at timestamp -- it anchored nothing new because nothing new existed to anchor. check_anchors itself was added in the commit whose subject is 'anchor: the verifier checks the anchors, and the stage says what one proves' (visible in git log as the parent chain immediately after 'anchor: the registers' dates stop resting on our own clock (D2 built)' and 'export: what this practice tells the house about itself'); every sentinel/darkocean job that has run since that commit landed has failed at the 'Verify provenance chain' step, and every one before it succeeded.
method: Read check_anchors in verify.py (lines 493-572, specifically the ledger-membership loop at 524-528) and manifests()/main() in tools/anchor.py (lines 76-91, 137-183). Compared the three workflow files' triggers and step order: .github/workflows/darkocean.yml ('Coverage-vs-Declaration reading' then 'Verify provenance chain' then 'Commit reading'), .github/workflows/sentinel.yml ('Notarize announced futures' then 'Verify provenance chain' then 'Commit observation'), .github/workflows/anchor.yml (separate cron job, checks out main and runs tools/anchor.py against whatever is already committed there). Read anchors/ledger.json directly: `python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('anchors/ledger.json')); print(d['counts']); [print(e['manifest'], e['state']) for e in d['anchors']]"` -- 6 manifests, all complete, none newer than 2026-08-09. Confirmed via `ls foreknown/snapshots darkocean/snapshots` that no directory newer than 2026-08-08/2026-08-09 exists, and via `grep '"step": "foreknown-notary-run"\|"step": "darkocean-run"' autonomy/log.jsonl` that the newest such entries are 2026-08-09T06:27:05Z (foreknown-notary-run) and 2026-08-09T05:36:36Z (darkocean-run), with none after. `git show a8b1510 -- anchors/ledger.json` shows the one commit since then touched only the generated_at field.
worth_watching_because: This is not a claim about the world the observatory watches -- it is a claim that the observatory itself has stopped watching. Every future in foreknown/registry.json, every drought window, every attention reading, every darkocean coverage figure is now frozen at its 2026-08-09 state and will stay frozen on every future scheduled run, because the check that gates commits (check_anchors) can never be satisfied by the same job that is trying to satisfy it -- the anchor that would cover a night's manifest cannot exist until after that manifest is committed, and commit cannot happen until the anchor exists. Unlike the sensor proposals in this directory, this is not a pattern that needs more nights to confirm: the mechanism is visible in the code as written, and two consecutive failed runs (2026-08-10, 2026-08-11) already match the predicted behaviour exactly, including the specific missing-manifest paths named in each run's own error output ('anchor ledger omits foreknown/snapshots/2026-08-11/manifest.json' and 'anchor ledger omits darkocean/snapshots/2026-08-10/manifest.json'). Left alone, this stays permanent, not intermittent -- there is no future night, however many attempts, in which a fresh manifest can already be in an anchor ledger that only ever anchors what is already on main.
